evidence: HfO2 films were deposited on the oxidized Si surface by showerhead-type ALD at a temperature of 300 °C. After standard cleaning, an ultrathin SiO2 layer with the thickness of ,1.5 nm was grown by radical-oxygen oxidation by low temperature treatment, prior to the HfO2 deposition. The precursors used for the Hf and the O sources were HfCl4 and H2O, respectively. The source temperatures were 170 °C for HfCl4 and 14.5 °C for H2O. One cycle of ALD-HfO2 growth consisted of an 800 ms pulse of HfCl4, followed by a 200 ms pulse of H2O, each carried by a flow of nitrogen and separated by 100 s. The purge time was extended to eliminate a CVD type of growth. The gas line for the final dose was separated in order to prevent interference by the two gases and the process pressure was 250 mTorr.
